### Fixed
- **The models Gateway reaches a served `LLMInferenceService`: the llm-d workload's network policy admits the workload's own port, 8000** (giantswarm/agent-platform#525; proof 1 of giantswarm/giantswarm#37639). The connectivity chart's `-model-serving-llmisvc-workload` CiliumNetworkPolicy admitted ingress on `modelServing.networkPolicy.predictor.port` — 8080, the classic `InferenceService` predictor's, the one port every shape's policy shared since #506 — while the workload pod the llm-d controller creates is reached on 8000 — the port KServe's `<name>-kserve-workload-svc` targets and the rendered HTTPRoute's backendRef names: the template's llm-d routing sidecar (`--port=8000 --vllm-port=8001`), vLLM's `main` on 8001 behind it. On gazelle (4.28.18, 2026-09-17 05:39Z, the first hands-free run of the proof to reach a Ready predictor) hubble showed the gateway's SYNs to the pod on 8000 policy-denied, and every `POST …/v1/chat/completions` with a person's id_token answered `503 upstream call failed: Connect: deadline has elapsed` (without a token 401: the JWT policy worked). Each pod shape now carries its port in the chart's one shape list (`agent-platform.modelServing.podShapes`): the classic predictor `predictor.port` (8080, unchanged), the llm-d workload the new **`modelServing.networkPolicy.llmisvcWorkload.port`** (8000), declared in both charts — the meta chart forwards its whole values tree to the connectivity release, so a connectivity-only default would have been shadowed by the meta chart's tree exactly as the #522 lists were (#524). Every rule that names the port renders per shape: the ingress from the callers and from the kubelet (cilium), the kubernetes-flavour ingress, and the kagent agents' egress, now one rule per shape on that shape's port instead of both shapes on 8080. `make verify-model-serving-policies` ties each shape's admitted port — in every one of those rules, as rendered from the connectivity defaults and from the values the meta chart forwards — to the port of the container the shape's fixture pod is reached on (`tests/fixtures/model-serving-llmisvc-workload-pod.yaml` gains the routing sidecar the pod is reached through on 8000; `main` keeps its 8001), refuses two fixtures on one port, and fails a render whose llm-d value is the classic port (the 4.28.18 shape) naming the shape; `make verify-meta` (`tests/verify-mirrored-values.py`) holds every `networkPolicy` `port` equal between the two charts next to the `fqdns` / `cidrs` lists, both model-serving ports required. **Every installation with model serving on gets two policy changes and no pod roll**: the llm-d workload's ingress moves to 8000, and the agents' egress splits into one rule per shape. The live half — `POST …/v1/chat/completions` with a person's id_token → 200 from the served model, without a token → 401 — is the proof's.
